data.narrative:
Seasats is a Series A-stage ocean and maritime technology company founded by Mike Flanigan, Dan Flanigan, Dylan Rodriguez, and Max Kramers. The company has raised approximately $40M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a narrow comp universe of two identifiable private peers—Bedrock Ocean and Havoc AI—with no public comparables available in the ocean and maritime frontier-tech sector.

Stage-progression analysis, the sole applicable quantitative method, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to seed/early transition. Using the $40M in total capital raised as a proxy valuation baseline yields an implied valuation of $80M. This method assumes Seasats demonstrates materially improved traction and de-risking relative to its entry valuation, a standard assumption at this funding stage.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $68M (low) to $92M (high), with a median point of $80M. The relatively narrow band reflects reliance on a single methodological input rather than consensus across multiple approaches. Key uncertainties include the absence of public market benchmarks for the ocean-tech sector, limited visibility into the financial and operational metrics of the two private comparables, and incomplete data on Seasats' revenue, customer concentration, or technical milestones. A more robust valuation would require either expansion of the comp set or introduction of discounted cash flow or venture capital method inputs.
